notes: METHOD RULE 1 VINDICATED — decisively. Unbracketed tags were not an edge case: (a) sunoaiwiki.com's canonical 'List of Metatags', the single most-copied Suno list in existence, presents EVERY tag WITHOUT brackets in a definition table; (b) the Japanese gen-ai-note list is 32 bare lowercase words; (c) enosentra.pe.kr (ko) lists all vocal/SFX tags unbracketed; (d) the DCinside (ko) vocal-style list — the only source carrying bare 'Narration' and 'Sprechgesang' — is entirely unbracketed. A bracket-only regex would have erased all four sources completely, including the best narration hits.

NEW FAILURE MODE FOUND — PARENTHESES. mylife-blog.com (ja) systematically encodes STRUCTURE tags in [ ] but VOCAL-PERFORMANCE tags in ( ): (Whispered), (Spoken Word), (Vocal Fry), (Staccato delivery). A bracket-only regex there does something worse than fail loudly — it silently returns a plausible-looking structure-tag list while dropping 100% of the vocal-delivery class. The Spanish SucDePoma onomatopoeia class (Chuka-chuka, Waah-Waaah-WAAH) is likewise fully bracket-free.

NARRATION LANE — best result is Russian, not Korean. gerwin.io lists [Narration], [Spoken Word] and [Whisper] as three DISTINCT bracketed voice-delivery tags. Bare [Narration] appears nowhere in the canonical Bark/Chirp list, and appears in only one other source I read (DCinside, unbracketed).

SPELLING IS UNSTABLE AND THAT IS THE FINDING. One Habr article alone uses [Spoken word], [Spoken words], AND [spoken voice]. Across sources whisper appears as [Whisper] / [whispers] / [Whispers] / Whispering / (Whispered) / [Whispered Vocals]. Female narrator appears as 'Female narrator' (unbracketed sentence-case, upstream) / [Female Narrator] / [female narrator]. Any exact-string matcher will undercount badly; normalize case, strip brackets/parens, and lemmatize before deduping.

[Female Narrator] IS REAL, but I still cannot attribute it to suno.wiki. I read it verbatim on three pages I actually fetched — brunch.co.kr (ko), note.com (ja), sunoprompt.com/ko — plus its unbracketed upstream form 'Female narrator' on sunoaiwiki.com. Per the brief I make no claim about the 403'd suno.wiki page. Related: [Male Narrator] appears on brunch.co.kr but is NOT in the canonical Bark list — likely a Korean-side extrapolation, so treat as unverified.

INFLATION CONFIRMED, matching the pattern flagged in the brief. sunometatagcreator.com advertises 2,596 tags (homepage category sum) / '1000+' (guide title); ~280-300 are actually written out, and even those are padded with combinatorial filler (every key, every chord quality, every time signature) rather than Suno-specific vocabulary. openmusicprompt claims '500+ verified' but writes out ~15 vocal tags amid category prose. Roughly 10:1 advertised-to-real on the worst offender.

SIZE ANTI-CORRELATES WITH NARRATION COVERAGE. The two largest advertised sites are the weakest on this lane: sunometatagcreator (2,596 claimed) has NO narrator/spoken-word/phone/radio tag at all, only [Whispered Vocals]. openmusicprompt (500+ claimed) has no [Female Narrator]. Meanwhile a single Russian blog post and one Korean game-forum thread carry the distinctive narration vocabulary. Do not prioritize sources by advertised size.

DERIVATIVE CLUSTER — do not treat as corroboration. sunoprompt.com/ko, vozart.ai, snonlyric.com/ru, and songshuhezi.com (zh) all reproduce the SAME canonical Bark v0 + Chirp v1 list (identical 35 Bark tags, identical genre ordering including the odd trailing [Uk]). songshuhezi explicitly self-describes as a translation of Suno's official docs. These four are one source in four languages; flagged derivative:true. The DCinside post also self-declares it compiled from suno.wiki + sunoaiwiki.com.

GRADE A_demo COUNT IS ZERO. Not one source in this sweep linked publicly playable audio isolating a specific tag. The Habr author links three finished songs but they are whole compositions, not tag demos; the DCinside post links only its two wiki sources. Every tag here is B_recited. The recited-vs-demonstrated gap remains completely unclosed on the narration lane.

KOREAN-LANGUAGE TAG BODIES EXIST but are localization artifacts, not evidence Suno accepts Korean. sunoaiwiki.com/ko machine-translates the tag text itself ([소개], [절], [코러스], [여성 보컬]). Every guide that discusses the question — Spanish, Russian, Japanese — states the opposite rule: keep brackets in English, write only lyrics in the local language. Treat the Korean-bodied tags as unverified and do not seed prompts from them without a controlled test.

COLON-QUALIFIER / DESCRIPTIVE-COMPOSITE CONVERGENCE. Four mutually independent sources in three languages converge on 'namespace: free-text payload' as the expressive form: Korean brunch ([Verse 1: Low-energy, Narrative]), Japanese mylife-blog ([Energy: Explosive], [Solo: Guitar]), Russian Plaan.ai ([Vocal Emotion: wistful, introspective]), English openmusicprompt ([Vocal Style: Whisper]). The Korean article's framing — V5 reads brackets as '편곡 지시서' (arrangement instruction sheets) — is the explicit statement of it. This independently corroborates the project's existing hypothesis that descriptive/composite brackets outperform bare labels; note it is still recited, not measured.

[Verse 1: Low-energy, Narrative] is a narration route with NO narrator keyword in it. Keyword-driven collection for this lane will systematically miss narration expressed as a delivery qualifier inside a structure tag. Future sweeps should grep for 'Narrative', 'Monotone', 'Sprechgesang', 'Vocal Fry', 'Staccato delivery' and colon-payloads, not just narrator/spoken/whisper.

REDDIT IS TOTALLY UNREACHABLE from this toolchain (5 distinct routes, all failed) and YouTube descriptions are unreachable because WebFetch cannot execute JS. Both are unread, NOT empty. Recovering them needs a different mechanism (authenticated API, or yt-dlp for YT). Zhihu/CSDN (403/521) are the largest known-unread Chinese caches and are the highest-value next target.
